policy: Complete for the enumerated public source families at this release. New files within those families are included automatically. The command manifest owns command grammar; canonical runtime/current schemas take precedence over portable guidance, whose historical command phrases are reference data only. Site-created tags, native element controls, enabled query types and dynamic content must additionally be read from the current site SiteGraph/Bricks context. Registered, inferred and target-verified capabilities are distinct. Unsupported or missing evidence must stop the affected handoff; never invent a tag, control, interaction or condition.

entries.value: Bricks remains page-design authority. DSA remains Surface/app authority. Theme authors may style/arrange DSA surfaces and may rely on semantic Bricks markers, but must not copy per-site Bricks element IDs.
Stable runtime marker for observed Bricks element roots. Never hardcode across sites.
Observed Bricks element type for registry/classification.
Canonical Bricks/page launcher target for a registered DSA module such as cart, profile, search, menu, saved, links, theme, ai, notifications, or ios-install.
Live Kiwe Saved capability hook for Wishlist/Bookmarks. Use dynamic Bricks IDs/titles/URLs in loops.
Optional saved-item metadata. Prefer Bricks dynamic tags such as {post_id}, {post_title}, {post_url}, and {featured_image}.
Starts the browser-notification preference journey only after explicit visitor click.
Optional notification status selector and real Kiwe topic hint.
Live light/dark mode control outside the Kiwe dock, synchronized with Kiwe/Bricks theme state.
Live contact action resolved from approved Kiwe Design Context. Prefer native Bricks links with the matching kiwe_*_url dynamic tag.
Optional short non-private WhatsApp starter message, encoded by Kiwe only after visitor activation.
Live public business-profile link resolved from the canonical DSA Links/Design Context record.
Marks preview/sample regions that should become Bricks query loops or dynamic binding plans.
Public Seam section meaning for page structure. Kiwe may read existing sections as menu-context fallback when configured heading TOC items are unavailable; do not add this solely for DSA Menu.
Bricks Filter Search element that DSA Search may bridge into.
Icon element: Kiwe DSA launcher module selector
Filter Search element: Use as DSA Search bridge
WooCommerce mini-cart: quantity stepper and Kiwe mini-cart controls
Product add-to-cart: DSA add-to-cart enhancer controls
Product upsells: linked products / FBT controls
Kiwe universal tokens are exported to Bricks global variables as kiwe-* variables.
Kiwe universal color tokens are exported to the Bricks color palette as Kiwe Universal.

Kiwe Seam framework classes are exported to Bricks global classes under Kiwe Seam categories. The expanded Seam Class Vocabulary is neutral/searchable: Bricks stores names/categories and designers attach visual styles there; Kiwe only ships CSS for true framework primitives/utilities.
Consume Kiwe tokens exported to Bricks variables.
Style DSA surfaces with universal kiwe-* and compatibility dsa-* tokens.
Design Bricks pages that contain semantic DSA launchers and live Kiwe Appsite capability attributes.
Use DSA Search bridge when Bricks owns the page query.
Do not parse or persist Bricks post meta from a theme.
Do not copy generated Bricks IDs between websites.
Do not replace Bricks query authority with DSA theme code.
Do not create alternate mini-cart/checkout/payment authority.
Do not recreate wishlist/bookmark, notification permission, theme toggle, or DSA launcher behavior in page JavaScript when live Kiwe attributes exist.
Payloads expose capabilities and state. Themes may rearrange them but must preserve action ownership and data attributes.
Kiwe owns screen data, behavior, accessibility, and geometry. Themes own visual arrangement by styling live AppShell and Seam hooks, not by inventing preview-only screen markup.
Protected metadata for tooling, diagnostics, and AI understanding only. Importable theme CSS should style documented [data-dsa-part] hooks and public Seam vocabulary instead.
Importable theme CSS that only styles broad roots, panels, buttons, and colors should be treated as a color skin rather than a full AppShell theme.

Supported screens are capabilities, not mandatory dock visibility. A full AppShell theme should provide resilient visual coverage for all registered core screens, while the Kiwe settings profile decides which screens/icons are visible for the current site.
A non-commerce news/editorial website should not automatically show cart, checkout, orders, downloads, or addresses.

A combined preview should show only the screens that match the brief, Kiwe settings profile, and site business model, but importable theme CSS must still degrade cleanly if a site owner later enables another registered module.
Notifications and AI are valid DSA surfaces when they use existing notification/AI payloads and keep action execution core-owned.
Key.kiwe, WordPress user, WooCommerce account when available
Orders, Downloads, Addresses, and Sign out may be rows, cards, pills, or stat blocks.
Do not clone logout/account actions without their data attributes.
The theme may show counts such as Orders, Saved, and Kiwe points when payloads expose them; missing counts must degrade to labels.
WooCommerce cart and DSA cart reconciliation
WooCommerce checkout route or DSA checkout surface gate
Do not create an independent remove button unless core exposes a data-dsa-cart-remove contract; current removal is quantity-to-zero through data-dsa-cart-quantity.

FBT is always a side-scrolling rail. Themes may restyle its cards but must preserve .dsa-cart-fbt[data-dsa-cart-fbt] and .dsa-cart-fbt__rail[data-dsa-cart-fbt-rail] as a horizontal overflow rail with snap behavior; do not reinterpret it as a stacked list or auto-fit grid.
Checkout presentation may move, but data-dsa-checkout-open must remain on the authoritative checkout CTA.
Submitting orders outside WooCommerce checkout contract
DSA Search REST and optional Bricks Filter Search bridge
assets/js/search.js plus shell placeholder in assets/js/surface.js
visual-profile shell registry in surface.js; behavior remains in search.js
DSA Search REST and Bricks bridge
Themes may rearrange the shell slots but must keep data-dsa-search-form, data-dsa-search-input, data-dsa-search-filters, data-dsa-search-alphabet, and data-dsa-search-results.
Bricks bridge reconciliation stays in assets/js/search.js; themes must not call Bricks filter utilities directly.
WordPress menus, DSA menu settings, page heading context engine
DSA Surface close and page scroll bridge

Page table-of-contents buttons are behavior-owned by the Surface close and page-scroll bridge. Themes may style or reposition them, but must keep data-dsa-menu-anchor on the clickable control and must not replace scrolling with theme JS.
DSA Saved Items service and Woo wishlist-like state

Identity, logo, site score, and commerce actions must consume Geometry Engine width and token colors. Do not let a score badge, logo, social link, Shop action, or Cart action shrink text below readability or become white-on-light / dark-on-dark in either color mode.
DSA notification preference service, Push/PWA journey, Key.kiwe identity when required
DSA Games engine, reward session service, and Surface game lifecycle
DSA game lifecycle and reward session gate
Themes may style the game shell, HUD, choices, messages, and canvas frame.
Themes must not replace the canvas engine, score loop, reward verification, attempt timing, or coupon issuance authority.
Standalone previews may use a static canvas poster or simple mock canvas; that preview code is never importable theme code.
DSA AI insight queue, notification history, cart/notification/action executors
Themes may rearrange AI presentation but must not execute AI actions directly.
Popout rendering and swipe/dismiss ownership remain core-owned.
Searchable generic class vocabulary for Bricks/global-class authoring. These class names are neutral handles, not starter visual recipes.

Public data-role values and seam-* role classes identify meaning for CSS, JavaScript, audits, Bricks, and AI tools. They do not apply starter card/button/modal visuals, padding, background, border, shadow, or radius. Build appearance with neutral Seam primitives, universal Kiwe/Seam tokens, and site CSS.

Builder-neutral Appsite capability hooks. Public page authors, Bricks layouts, block themes, and AI-generated HTML may use these attributes to call Kiwe-owned runtime journeys without recreating Kiwe behavior.

Use these attributes only on real interactive controls or semantic page regions. Preserve visible UI and add the smallest capability hook that matches the intent. Never create duplicate JavaScript authority for saved items, notifications, AppShell screens, theme switching, cart, checkout, auth, search, service workers, focus trapping, or browser history.
Open a registered Kiwe DSA/AppShell screen from a page/header/Bricks/custom control. The value theme toggles light/dark mode instead of opening a sheet.
Toggle the nearest item into Kiwe Saved. Use wishlist for WooCommerce product controls, bookmark for articles/pages, and auto only when the context is unambiguous.
Stable post/product ID, recommended in Bricks query loops.
Optional saved-item title override. Kiwe otherwise reads the nearest card heading.
Optional saved-item URL override. Kiwe otherwise reads the nearest card link or current URL.
Optional saved-item image URL. Kiwe otherwise reads the nearest card image.
Start the browser-notification preference journey after an explicit visitor click. Kiwe never prompts during a protected flow.
Optional CSS selector for an on-page live-status element that receives the current notification-permission message.
Optional topic hint for the notification preference screen. Use only real site topics exposed by Kiwe.
Advanced direct browser-permission request for a real visitor-click control. Prefer data-kiwe-notifications unless the UI is explicitly asking for native permission now.
Toggle Kiwe/Bricks light-dark mode from a page/header/Bricks/custom control without adding the dock theme icon.
Optional selector for a status element that receives the current light/dark state label.
Turn a real link or button into a contact action backed by the approved Kiwe Design Context. Kiwe resolves the destination; page markup must not duplicate phone, email, WhatsApp, or address values.
Chat on WhatsApp
Optional human-visible WhatsApp starter message. Kiwe URL-encodes it only after a visitor activates the control. Do not place private data or secrets here.
Prefer a Bricks-native link whose URL is {kiwe_store_phone_url}; retain data-kiwe-contact="phone" as semantic capability metadata.
Prefer a Bricks-native link whose URL is {kiwe_store_email_url}; retain data-kiwe-contact="email" as semantic capability metadata.
Prefer a Bricks-native link whose URL is {kiwe_whatsapp_url}; data-kiwe-contact-message may add a prefilled message at runtime.

Prefer a Bricks-native link whose URL is {kiwe_directions_url}. For a Bricks Map element, compose its native address control from the kiwe_store_address_* dynamic tags instead of embedding a map iframe.
Open the selected public business profile from Kiwe Design Context/DSA Links. Use only on a real link or button; Kiwe ignores unknown networks and missing URLs.
Expose real page sections to Kiwe Menu context without hidden duplicate anchors. Kiwe prefers semantic sections, then falls back to admin-selected heading levels.
Marks a source region whose preview/sample cards should become a Bricks query loop or dynamic binding plan.
Marks a repeated sample card or field that belongs to a named Kiwe dynamic binding plan.

Reuse the Home-screen install journey from a semantic button or link. A configured store/download URL takes precedence; otherwise use browser-supported installation or honest platform instructions. Available from RC393; verify current target capability. A click is install intent, not a confirmed download or notification consent.
<button type="button" data-dsa-install-pwa="android" aria-label="Install Android app">Install app</button>
Optional wrapper around install-only copy and attributed install buttons. Setup App hides this whole group when Show app install buttons is off; never wrap unrelated footer content.
Future Web Share / copy-link capability for products, posts, offers, and pages.
Future recently-viewed product/post rail and personalization signal.
Future author, brand, topic, category, or product-subscription follow intent.
Future safe context handoff to Kiwe AI from a selected section/card without exposing private data.
Future lightweight rating, helpful/not helpful, or report-an-issue intent.
Future coupon, bundle, FBT, or personalization trigger that remains Woo/Kiwe-owned.

Defines which public Seam classes Kiwe DSA itself may apply inside live sheets/screens. Normal WordPress pages and Bricks layouts may use the full public Seam vocabulary; this map is specifically for Kiwe AppShell internals where generic classes can accidentally alter geometry.
Runtime may add the public seam-* class to existing DSA markup because visual impact is low and reviewed.
Runtime annotates the role with protected data-seam-* metadata only. This preserves AppShell isolation from site CSS even when core Seam role classes are headless.
Runtime/state authority only. Themes and Seam must not create behavior for this concern.
Text-only role; existing DSA selectors already own surface typography and color.
Text-only helper; safe for muted supporting copy.
Numeric/text-only helper; tabular numeric styling is compatible with DSA price landmarks.
AppShell keeps card semantics on protected data-seam-* metadata so site CSS cannot accidentally style live DSA internals.
AppShell keeps button semantics protected so site CSS cannot override DSA controls.
AppShell keeps field/input semantics protected because Profile, Key.kiwe, checkout, and validation states are authority-owned.
AppShell keeps media semantics protected because DSA media geometry is screen-specific.
AppShell keeps badge semantics protected so site CSS cannot alter notification/status badges.
AppShell keeps nav semantics protected because dock and context navigation use Geometry Engine variables.
AppShell keeps action-row semantics protected because action placement is panel/dock/context-owned.
AppShell keeps form semantics protected because Profile, Key.kiwe, checkout, and notification forms are authority-owned.
AppShell keeps field semantics protected because validation, account, and checkout fields are authority-owned.
AppShell keeps modal semantics protected because DSA sheet/screen geometry owns this surface.
Kiwe DSA uses data-seam-* shadow metadata on live AppShell panels so tools can understand framework roles without generic Seam CSS restyling those panels.
Use public data-role/data-flow/classes for normal page markup. Do not add data-seam-* manually unless writing Kiwe runtime/core integration code.
Optional manifest note for token usage. Live design-token profile overrides belong in theme-package.json under settings.tokens using official Kiwe universal token names.

Safe theme preset. Kiwe imports only the style, dock, dsa_theme, visual_effects, tokens, and screens subsets. tokens may contain official Kiwe universal design-token overrides and safe Bricks global theme-style metadata. screens may contain presentation/copy labels for registered panels; it may not contain behavior, JavaScript, endpoints, or state authority.
Optional design-token profile shared by live DSA theme CSS, Seam website CSS, and Bricks global theme style. Override names must be official Kiwe universal token names.

Official Kiwe universal token overrides only, for example color-brand, color-accent, color-surface, color-text, font-display, font-body, type-h1, type-h2, leading-tight, space-md, radius-lg, shadow-md.
Safe Bricks global theme-style metadata. Kiwe may export typography, colors, links, and site background only.

Optional live-intended presentation/copy defaults for registered Kiwe DSA screens/sheets. This is the same lane manually editable in Kiwe > Theme > DSA screen/sheet copy. It may rename labels, titles, helper text, empty states, and safe CTA labels only. It must not contain products, orders, saved items, profile identity, social URLs, menu items, search results, notification state, AI messages/actions, checkout URLs, JavaScript, endpoints, or behavior authority.

approved browser-runnable HTML/CSS/JS and exact SiteGraph evidence when cited
builder-neutral semantic contract, exact source fingerprints and proof ledger
participating browser AI under the SEAM command contract
complete accepted pre-existing HTML/CSS/JS project without a strict SEAM Map, plus assets and SiteGraph whenever real site fields are requested
kiwe.bricks-bindings.v1 graph and binding report only; approved raw project remains unchanged; never Bricks JSON
explicit submission through the seam.kiwe application UI or API
complete accepted HTML/CSS/JS project, assets and either a strict validated kiwe.seam-map.v1 or optional legacy kiwe.bricks-bindings.v1
native Bricks page/header/footer/popup templates plus conversion evidence
only when the calibrated Bricks profile proves no native equivalent
the same complete rendered source evidence used by conversion
one Framework Profile, profile-dependent templates, real dependency package and integration audit
actual compiled native templates/Profile, referenced real bytes and source-resource reports
separate authorized Kiwe Framework review, supported native Media, compatible shared styles, guarded remapping and draft templates
preserve newer edits and reusable Media; no automatic publication or permanent media deletion
measured report or corrected same-lane artifact with before/after evidence
preserve the accepted design; dark mode may deliberately coordinate brand, accent, surface and text roles without collapsing every surface to black
last accepted artifact plus failure evidence
stacking speculative patches on the failed output
Raw conversion never injects or requires Seam Framework.
Framework is an explicit option, not a command or redesign.
Visual quality and the accepted design take priority; consolidate only equivalent values and meanings while preserving page/scoped values and script-owned variables.
Real asset bytes and exact native references determine the compiler package; AI notes, filenames, hashes and IDs are not proof of assets or native installation.
A missing Framework Profile fails closed and templates never depend on variable fallbacks.
Browser AI may author source design and binding intent but never production Bricks JSON or Framework Profile data.
/convert /bricks never emits Bricks JSON; seam.kiwe compilation is a separate explicit application action.
Strict SEAM Map conversion never infers dynamic, commerce, editorial, interaction or conditional meaning; missing, stale, duplicated, unproven or unresolved stitches fail closed.
SEAM Map is builder-neutral conversion context and does not apply Seam Framework or influence art direction.
Visual confidence is evidence based and never a universal fixed percentage.
Source defects are preserved in 1:1 conversion and reported separately.
No project-specific selector, brand, layout or route rule enters compiler core.
Preview receipt and Seam source handoff
AI authoring evidence. This never grants native save or production authority; the compiler independently validates the actual project and target.
Dry-run, non-mutating plan that turns a validated Kiwe Bricks binding plan into an admin-reviewed Bricks apply sequence.
Read-only binding plan that maps an approved Kiwe website/page handoff to Bricks query loops, dynamic data, Kiwe launchers, and review items.
Must indicate human review or a trusted Kiwe/Bricks adapter. The plan itself does not mutate WordPress.
Lean Bricks theme-style JSON for Bricks' Theme Styles manager. This is not a Kiwe Framework profile, not a Bricks template, and not a DSA/AppShell theme package.
Standalone Kiwe Framework design-token profile. Imports under Kiwe > Framework and contains settings.tokens only.
Machine-readable, user-approved preflight emitted before /ideate changes a supplied project.
Closed, marker-only semantic contract produced during /ideate and consumed deterministically by seam.kiwe.

Public field definitions only; no values. Current-site dynamicBindings additionally owns record, group, collection and configured commerce tags. Private/planning fields are never inferred from matching labels.
Kiwe content-free compiler calibration profile v1
Seam compiler package byte inventory v1

Sorted UTF-8 path + NUL + sha256:hex + LF nativeMember rows produce sourceHash. Hashes identify bytes, not a trusted compiler signer. Target revalidation, permission and current-state guards remain mandatory. Only listed members are inputs; a single optional portable framework manifest may accompany this inventory without execution authority.
Seam compiler dependency ownership review v1

Registered means available in the source inventory, not automatic conversion or target verification. Current target calibration/SiteGraph is required. This reference grants no executable-code authority.

Fixed public artwork and native Bricks icon tags only. App icons/actions require RC393 or current target evidence. Artwork does not establish app-store enrollment, installation or notification consent.
